title: College & Early Independence

myths.myth: Asking for consent is awkward and kills the mood.
myths.truth: Asking is normal, attractive and non-negotiable.
myths.explanation: Clarity beats assumption every single time.

myths.myth: A drunk or pressured 'yes' still counts.
myths.truth: Consent must be free, sober enough and willing.
myths.explanation: Incapacity isn't agreement.

myths.myth: Once you're together, consent is assumed.
myths.truth: It's checked each time, every time.
myths.explanation: A relationship isn't a blanket yes.

myths.myth: They didn't say no, so it was fine.
myths.truth: The absence of 'no' isn't a 'yes'.
myths.explanation: Consent is the presence of an enthusiastic yes.

myths.myth: If they seem nice online, they're safe to meet anywhere.
myths.truth: Meet in public, tell a friend, trust your gut.
myths.explanation: Online charm isn't verification.

myths.myth: You owe a date something for their time or money.
myths.truth: You owe no one your body — ever.
myths.explanation: A meal isn't a contract.

myths.myth: Ghosting and breadcrumbing are just modern dating; deal with it.
myths.truth: You can set standards and walk away.
myths.explanation: Respect is a baseline, not a bonus.

myths.myth: Sending nudes is expected once you match.
myths.truth: It's always your choice; pressure is a red flag.
myths.explanation: 'No' is a complete sentence.

myths.myth: Intensity — jealousy, drama — means it's real love.
myths.truth: Calm, trust and respect are the real thing.
myths.explanation: Chaos isn't chemistry.

myths.myth: Good couples never fight.
myths.truth: They fight fair and then repair.
myths.explanation: Conflict handled well actually builds trust.

myths.myth: Love means losing yourself in someone.
myths.truth: Healthy love leaves room for two whole people.
myths.explanation: You don't have to disappear to belong.

myths.myth: Leaving a bad relationship is failure.
myths.truth: Walking away from harm is strength.
myths.explanation: Staying isn't a virtue when it costs you.

myths.myth: Going to a clinic means something's wrong with you.
myths.truth: Routine sexual-health care is normal adult self-care.
myths.explanation: Prevention is smart, not shameful.

myths.myth: Contraception is the woman's department.
myths.truth: It's a shared, informed decision.
myths.explanation: Both people carry it.

myths.myth: Doctors will judge or report you.
myths.truth: You have a right to confidential, respectful care.
myths.explanation: Knowing that right helps you ask.

myths.myth: If you're embarrassed, just skip the check-up.
myths.truth: Awkwardness passes; untreated issues don't.
myths.explanation: Your future self will thank you.

myths.myth: Men are naturally better with money.
myths.truth: Money skills are learned, not gendered.
myths.explanation: Anyone can budget, save and invest.

myths.myth: Letting a partner control the money is romantic.
myths.truth: Financial independence protects you.
myths.explanation: Access to your own money is freedom.

myths.myth: Talking about money is rude.
myths.truth: Money conversations prevent money problems.
myths.explanation: Clarity beats silence.

myths.myth: You'll sort out savings 'later'.
myths.truth: Small habits early compound hugely.
myths.explanation: Time is your biggest asset.

myths.myth: Everyone else has it figured out; you're the only one struggling.
myths.truth: Most people are quietly finding their feet too.
myths.explanation: The highlight reel isn't real life.

myths.myth: Therapy or counselling is only for a crisis.
myths.truth: Support helps before things break.
myths.explanation: Maintenance beats emergency repair.

myths.myth: Loneliness means something's wrong with you.
myths.truth: It's a signal, not a flaw.
myths.explanation: Connection is built, not just found.

myths.myth: Asking for help will make people think less of you.
myths.truth: It usually deepens trust.
myths.explanation: Vulnerability is human.

myths.myth: By now you should know exactly what you want.
myths.truth: Most people figure it out by trying.
myths.explanation: Clarity comes from doing, not waiting.

myths.myth: Everyone else is ahead of you.
myths.truth: There's no shared starting line.
myths.explanation: Comparison steals time you could use.

myths.myth: Changing direction means you wasted time.
myths.truth: Pivots build range, not regret.
myths.explanation: Very few careers are straight lines.

myths.myth: Rejection means you're not good enough.
myths.truth: Rejection is data, not a verdict.
myths.explanation: It redirects you more than it defines you.

myths.myth: Equality's basically done — relax.
myths.truth: Gaps in pay, safety and unpaid load persist.
myths.explanation: Progress isn't the same as finished.

myths.myth: Confident women are arrogant; quiet men are weak.
myths.truth: Confidence and gentleness suit everyone.
myths.explanation: The double standard is the problem.

myths.myth: Speaking up about sexism makes you difficult.
myths.truth: Naming it is how things change.
myths.explanation: Comfort isn't worth more than fairness.

myths.myth: Workplace harassment is just part of the job.
myths.truth: The POSH Act gives you the right to a safe workplace.
myths.explanation: Every workplace must have a complaints committee.

myths.myth: As a renter or consumer, you have no power.
myths.truth: Tenancy and consumer laws protect you.
myths.explanation: Knowing them is leverage.

myths.myth: What you post online can't come back on you.
myths.truth: Digital footprints and data rights are real.
myths.explanation: Privacy needs active management.

myths.myth: Rights are too complicated to bother with.
myths.truth: A few key ones cover most situations.
myths.explanation: Basic literacy prevents big losses.

capstone.name: Standing on My Own
capstone.landing: Sticker-book spread of every Ch.6 sticker earned; freshly erased 'adult' myths glowing as ghosts under their truths; a 'Standing on My Own' badge; Lensy raising a mug onward to Chapter 7.

canvasFeel: Adult/dark — the corridor flips. Paper becomes deep ink (#15131F) on a faint light dot texture; Equal Violet, Insight Teal (UN) and Grow Coral (RE) glow against the dark; sticky-note myths become softly lit cards. Wry-but-kind register (knowing, warm, dry, never preachy). Leaner than teen chapters. Tap struck myth -> UN erases -> RE writes -> sticker may drop; consent & rights nodes link out to real helplines/committees.
